sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Missouri City, TX?
sections.html:
Yes. Homeowners in Missouri City sell for cash in a matter of weeks when they skip listing prep, showings and buyer financing. The trade is price: a direct buyer discounts the offer to cover repairs and risk, so compare it against a realistic listing net before you decide.

Missouri City sits about twenty miles southwest of downtown Houston along U.S. Highway 90A and State Highway 6, in northeast Fort Bend County and southwest Harris County, according to the Handbook of Texas. That split matters when you sell, because the county line decides which appraisal district and tax office hold your records.

Most sellers here reach for a fast sale for one of a few reasons:

  • A job move that makes carrying two households impractical.
  • An inherited house nobody wants to maintain.
  • Deferred repairs, foundation or roof, that would scare off financed buyers.
  • A tax bill or mortgage that has fallen behind.
  • A tenant-occupied house the owner is tired of managing.

sections.h2: What is Missouri City like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Missouri City is a Houston commuter city with a long residential history. Two Houston investors bought four square miles here in 1890 and advertised the land in St. Louis, and the town took its name from that pitch. It was incorporated on March 13, 1956, and moved to a council-manager government in 1974, per the Handbook of Texas entry.

The same entry notes that most residents commute to jobs in Houston and that the city is served by the Fort Bend Independent School District. A house near a shaded older street, a newer subdivision, or a lot inside a municipal utility district can each carry a different tax picture, so describe your exact address when you ask for an offer.

The city is still investing in its own streets. Its fiscal 2027 budget announcement lists street reconstruction on Robinson Road Phase II, La Quinta Drive south of Cartwright, Masters Lane, Meadow Creek Drive, Oakview Drive, Westwood Circle and North Evelyn Circle, plus drainage work at Pine Meadow and Gregory and McLain. If your street appears on a project list, ask the city when work is scheduled, because buyers notice torn-up roads.

sections.h2: How much property tax does a Missouri City homeowner pay?
sections.html:
The tax bill is stacked from several taxing units, and the city publishes the breakdown on its Tax Information page. The table below copies the rates per $100 of assessed value as that page prints them for tax years 2025 and 2024.

sections.h2: What is the adopted city tax rate for fiscal 2027?
sections.html:
The City Council adopted a rate of $0.578363 per $100 of taxable value for fiscal 2027, up from $0.570825, according to the city's September 22, 2026 press release. The city says the increase is in the debt service portion and the maintenance and operations portion did not change.

The same release says voters approved an $85.85 million bond program on November 2, 2021, and puts the median homestead taxable value at $310,147 with an estimated city bill of $1,793.78. Those are the city's own figures for its portion only, not the whole bill. County, school and district rates are set separately.

The Tax Information page also lists a combined sales tax rate of 8.25 percent for the city.

sections.h2: Who appraises and bills my Missouri City property?
sections.html:
It depends on the county. Fort Bend properties go through the Fort Bend Central Appraisal District, and Harris County properties go through the Harris County Appraisal District, based on the city's notice to taxpayers.

  • Fort Bend Central Appraisal District: 2801 B.F. Terry Boulevard, Rosenberg, TX 77471.
  • Harris County Appraisal District: 13013 Northwest Freeway, Houston, TX 77040-6305.
  • Fort Bend tax office, Missouri City Annex Branch: 307 Texas Parkway, Suite 113, 281-261-2886.
  • Fort Bend tax office, Sienna Annex: 5855 Sienna Springs Way, 832-471-4140.

Under the Comptroller's calendar, values are set as of January 1 and a tax lien attaches that day, so taxes follow the property through a sale. Most protests are due May 15 or 30 days after the value notice arrives, whichever is later.

sections.h2: Does a delinquent tax bill or foreclosure change my options?
sections.html:
Yes, and both put a clock on a sale. Under the Comptroller's payment page, unpaid taxes are delinquent after January 31 and a six percent penalty plus one percent interest begins on February 1. Interest keeps running at one percent a month.

For a mortgage in default, the State Law Library explains that a homeowner has 20 days after the default notice to catch up, and the notice of sale must come at least 21 days before the auction. Foreclosure auctions are held on the first Tuesday of a month. A cash sale that closes ahead of that date can leave you with whatever equity exists instead of a foreclosure on your record.

Any sale payoff, whether back taxes or a lender balance, comes out of your proceeds at closing, so ask the title company for the payoff figures before you accept a price.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale cost compared with listing in Missouri City?
sections.html:
A listing costs agent commissions, repairs, carrying costs and time on the market, while a cash sale usually costs a lower price and little else. Which one nets you more depends on the condition of the house and how fast you need to close.

  • Listing: pay for repairs, cleaning, staging and months of mortgage, tax and utilities, then negotiate inspection requests.
  • Cash sale: the buyer takes the house as is, you pick the closing date, and there are no financing delays.
  • Both: a Texas deed is recorded with the county clerk, and the clerk's fee schedule starts at $5 for the first page and $4 for each added page, per the County Clerk Manual.

Ask for the offer in writing, with the closing date and who pays for title work, and get a second number from a listing agent for comparison.

sections.h2: How do I handle a tenant, an inherited house or a probate sale?
sections.html:
Each one adds a step before you can hand over keys. A tenant must be removed through a notice to vacate and, if needed, a justice court case. A house that passed by will may need the will admitted to probate, which the State Law Library says is generally possible within four years of death.

  • Tenant: written notice to vacate is usually at least three days unless the lease says otherwise.
  • Small estate: the affidavit route covers estates of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead, and it needs court approval.
  • No court filing yet: an affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement, and buyers do not have to accept it.

If the owner has died and nobody has opened probate, talk to a Texas attorney before signing anything.

faqs.q: How fast can a Missouri City house close for cash?
faqs.a: Often within a few weeks, because there is no lender underwriting. The real pace depends on title work, a Fort Bend or Harris County lien search, and whether you need extra time to move. Ask for a closing date in writing.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with if my Missouri City home is near the county line?
faqs.a: Your address decides. Missouri City spans Fort Bend and Harris counties, so the appraisal district and tax office are Fort Bend's or Harris County's depending on the parcel. Look up your account number on your tax bill to see which one applies.

faqs.q: Is the Missouri City tax rate for fiscal 2027 adopted?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's September 22, 2026 press release says the council adopted $0.578363 per $100 of taxable value for fiscal 2027. That is the city's portion only and excludes county, school and district rates.

faqs.q: Do I owe taxes if I sell partway through the year?
faqs.a: The tax lien attaches on January 1, so the year's bill belongs to the property and gets settled at closing. The title company usually prorates it between buyer and seller. Check the settlement statement line by line.

faqs.q: Where can I find my Missouri City property's tax breakdown?
faqs.a: Start with the city's Tax Information page for the unit rates, then your county appraisal district for your parcel's value and exemptions. The Fort Bend tax office branch on Texas Parkway can answer billing questions by phone.
